title: Ruganzu Ndori restores the kingdom
description: By tradition Ruganzu II Ndori refounds the Nyiginya kingdom and begins its expansion across the hills.

title: Accession of Rwabugiri
description: Kigeli IV Rwabugiri begins a reign of conquest and centralisation that gives the kingdom roughly its present extent.

title: Götzen meets Rwabugiri
description: A German officer is received at the royal court, the first European to cross the country, which Germany has already been assigned on paper.

title: Rucunshu coup
description: The queen mother Kanjogera and her brothers overthrow the new king and put the young Yuhi V Musinga on the throne.

title: First Catholic mission
description: The White Fathers found a mission at Save, the start of a church that becomes central to colonial society.

title: Kigali founded
description: The German resident Richard Kandt sets up his headquarters on a hill in the centre of the country.

title: Belgian troops take Kigali
description: Forces from the Belgian Congo occupy Rwanda during the First World War, and Belgium rules it for the next forty-six years.

title: Belgian mandate
description: The League of Nations entrusts Rwanda and Burundi to Belgium, which governs them through the existing monarchies.

title: Musinga deposed
description: The Belgians remove the king, who had refused baptism, and replace him with his son Mutara III Rudahigwa.

title: Ruzagayura famine
description: Drought and wartime requisitions bring a famine that kills a large part of the population and drives many to emigrate.

title: Bahutu Manifesto
description: Nine Hutu intellectuals publish a demand for an end to Tutsi dominance of power, land and education.

title: Rwandan Revolution
description: An attack on a Hutu sub-chief sets off violence in which Tutsi homes are burned, many are killed and tens of thousands flee abroad.

title: Republic proclaimed at Gitarama
description: Local officials meeting with Belgian approval abolish the monarchy, a step confirmed by referendum in September.

title: Independence
description: Rwanda becomes independent from Belgium as a republic under Grégoire Kayibanda.

title: Bugesera invasion
description: Tutsi exiles attack from Burundi and are beaten back, and thousands of Tutsi inside the country are killed in reprisal.

title: Habyarimana seizes power
description: The army chief Juvénal Habyarimana overthrows Kayibanda and rules for twenty-one years.

title: Rwandan Patriotic Front invades
description: An army of Tutsi exiles crosses from Uganda, beginning the civil war.

title: Arusha Accords
description: The government and the Rwandan Patriotic Front agree to share power, a settlement that Hutu hardliners reject.

title: President's aircraft shot down
description: A missile brings down the aircraft carrying Habyarimana and the president of Burundi as it approaches Kigali airport.

title: Genocide against the Tutsi
description: Soldiers, militias and civilians begin the organised killing of Tutsi and of moderate Hutu, murdering at least half a million people in about a hundred days.

title: Rwandan Patriotic Front takes Kigali
description: The rebel army captures the capital and within two weeks controls the country, ending the genocide while about two million Hutu flee abroad.

title: Kibeho massacre
description: Soldiers of the new army kill thousands of people while closing a camp for the internally displaced.

title: Paul Kagame becomes president
description: The commander who led the Rwandan Patriotic Front, already the country's effective leader, takes the presidency.

title: New constitution
description: Voters approve a constitution that ends the post-genocide transition and bans parties based on ethnicity.

title: Rwanda joins the Commonwealth
place: Port of Spain, Trinidad and Tobago
description: A country with no historical tie to Britain is admitted, part of its turn away from France.

title: Term-limit referendum
description: Voters approve changes that allow Paul Kagame to stand for further terms.
